title: Qualities of Dyspnea and their pathophysiological pattern regarding COPD patients
summary: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a globally widespread and severe disease characterized by chronic airway constriction and inflammation. One of the main complaints of COPD patients is shortness of breath, which can have a significant impact on everyday life and quality of life. This is a heterogeneous symptom that can occur in different qualities, such as tightness in the chest, rapid breathing or the feeling of not getting enough air. The different qualities may indicate different underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. Identifying these pathophysiological patterns and assigning them to the corresponding qualities can enable a more precise characterization of the disease and targeted treatment.

interventions.name:
In a period from 10/23 to probably 01/25, patients who are treated either as inpatients or outpatients at the Cologne-Merheim Lung Clinic (KdSK) and suffer from COPD GOLD II-IV will be examined. 
As part of the recruitment process, the patients' demographic data is collected and a survey is conduct

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Previously known or newly diagnosed COPD according to the definition of obstruction according to the bronchospasmolysis test Z value < -1.64
- Smoker/ex-smoker with at least 20 pack-years
- Consent to data protection and patient information
- Willingness to answer the questionnaires in full
- Linguistic and cognitive abilities to answer the questionnaires
Exclusion criteria:
- Patient age < 18 years
- Alexia, deafness
- Patients incapable of giving consent, without deputy legal guardianship
- Exacerbation within the last 2 weeks
- Eosinophils > 300/microliter
- Alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency
- FENO values > 40 ppm
- Pre-existing conditions (asthma, bronchiectasis, ILD, bronchial CA, other pneumological diseases)
